# Binary carrier with nominal results and exact array tails

A public static method retains two distinct method formals in Map<K,V>,
independent String contexts, a String[] tail and an opaque String result.
The varargs call receives its exact array; an owned convenience method creates
its original empty array. Four frozen routes compare 96 cases twice with source
and SDK providers. Every original entry, Signature, Exceptions attribute and
methodless class is audited after compiling all output. Observers check raw and
null maps, hostile/unmodifiable inputs, exact array identity and contents,
context identity, partial writes, callbacks, result identity and exact failures.
Six wrong programs and Code-preserving Signature controls guard the proof.
Only authored fixtures execute.
